scenario: [LNUL.8.4] the two missings are distinct, and `has()` is the only thing that separates them. Drives the other half of the pair. Three conjuncts, each pinning a different sentence of the clause: `p.body.nulled is null` — a present JSON null READS AS null, and `is` is total over it ([LNUL.4.9]), which a soft-fail marker makes answer FALSE; `p.body.five is not null` — the control, without which a projection answering `null` for every leaf would pass; and `has(p.body.nulled)` — a leaf-read of a present JSON null is a VALUE, so has() must still say the key is there. The dead rule is the other missing: an unresolved path also reads as `null` but has() must say FALSE, which is the distinction the clause exists to state and the reason `builtin_json_has` reads presence off the node pointer rather than off the projected value. ONLY MEANINGFUL BESIDE LNUL.8.4a, which drives `??` over the same document.
rules_ds:
schema Payload scope logical:
    body: Json key

rule is_null_reads_the_present_null:
    Payload p where p.body.nulled is null and p.body.five is not null and has(p.body.nulled)
->
    log critical "is-null-ok"

rule has_refuses_the_unresolved_path:
    Payload p where has(p.body.missing)
->
    log critical "has-missing"
